summary: iter459 — Order Cancellation & Resolution Workflow (P0). ALL BACKEND (21/21 pytest pass in test_iter459_order_cancellation.py, junitxml iter120.xml) + ALL FRONTEND surfaces from review request PASSED against the live preview. BACKEND: (1) GET /api/orders/cancel-reasons returns exactly 6 groups {inventory, production, customer, mutual, shipping, other} with 16 total reasons. (2) Maker cancel guards — invalid reason → 400, 'other' with 1-char explanation → 400, missing order → 404, kiln-and-clay JWT on iron-and-oak order → 403, order_status='fulfilled' → 409, no auth → 401/403. (3) Refund-failure path — POST /api/maker/orders/cs_test_agent1/cancel with equipment-failure against fake Stripe session → 409 'Refund failed — order NOT canceled: Could not load Stripe session'. Verified cancellation.status=='refund_failed', timeline events include cancel_requested + refund_failed, order_status stays 'pending' (NOT canceled). Duplicate cancel attempt while refund_failed → 409 (ACTIVE_STATUSES lock holds). (4) Admin reopen — POST /api/admin/orders/cs_test_agent1/cancellation/reopen → 200 {ok:true, order_status:'pending'}, cancellation cleared to None. Reopen on simulated cancellation.status='canceled_refunded' → 409. (5) Admin no-refund cancel — mode='no_refund' with internal_note='' → 400 (mandatory note); with 'resolved via chargeback' (>=5 chars) → 200, cancellation.status=='canceled_no_refund', order_status='canceled', timeline sequence [cancel_requested, inventory_restored, buyer_notified, closed] verified, product mountain-range-silhouette in_stock 4→6 (qty 2 restored). Duplicate cancel → 409. (6) restore_inventory:false on cs_test_agent2 → timeline event 'inventory_not_restored' present, 'inventory_restored' absent, product stock unchanged. (7) PATCH /api/admin/orders/cs_test_agent1/cancellation {reason:'buyer-requested'} → 200, cancellation.reason updated, timeline event 'reason_edited' pushed; invalid reason → 400; unknown session_id → 404. (8) GET /api/admin/orders/cancellation-stats returns paid_orders(7), canceled_orders(1), cancellation_rate, top_reasons[{reason,label,count}], refund_total, avg_hours_to_cancel, initiators{}, by_maker[]. No auth → 403. (9) GET /api/maker/orders (iron-and-oak JWT) rows include 'cancellation' + 'order_total' fields. FRONTEND MAKER (/maker/dashboard?tab=orders with cm_maker_jwt = iron-and-oak): orders-list renders, each order row has data-testid='order-actions-{sid}' ⋮ button; menu opens with data-testid order-action-message-*, order-action-cancel-*, order-action-report-*. Clicking Cancel opens data-testid='cancel-order-modal' with cancel-nudge-step + cancel-contact-buyer-btn. Continue → cancel-form-step with cancel-reason-select (grouped options), cancel-note, cancel-no-restore checkbox, cancel-confirm-btn text 'Cancel & refund $84.00'. Selecting 'other' reveals cancel-explanation textarea. Submitting equipment-failure on fake Stripe session surfaces data-testid='cancel-error' with 'Refund failed — order NOT canceled: Could not load Stripe session. The order remains open — our team has been alerted.' After refresh the order shows data-testid='order-status-refund-failed-cs_test_agent1' pill. Cancelled order cs_test_cxl2 shows data-testid='order-status-cancelled-cs_test_cxl2' pill; the ⋮ menu on a cancelled order does NOT include order-action-cancel (correctly hidden). Expanding cxl2 reveals data-testid='order-timeline-cs_test_cxl2' with 'Order placed → Payment received → Cancellation requested → Inventory restored (2 units) → Buyer notified → Closed → Reason edited by admin'. FRONTEND ADMIN (/admin/dashboard?tab=orders with cm_admin_jwt): data-testid='cancellation-stats' strip renders exactly 5 cards (14.3% Cancellation rate, 1 Cancelled orders, $0.00 Refund total, 0 Avg hrs to cancel, top reason 'Buyer requested cancellation'). data-testid='orders-list-admin' renders. cs_test_cxl2 shows data-testid='order-cancellation-cs_test_cxl2' badge with 'canceled no refund · buyer-requested · by admin:team@craftersmarket.org · note: Chargeback CB-9931' plus data-testid='order-edit-reason-cs_test_cxl2' + data-testid='order-reopen-cs_test_cxl2' links. cs_test_agent1 (during test) shows REFUND FAILED pill + edit-reason + reopen links. Open orders show 5 data-testid='order-cancel-norefund-btn-*' '⊘ No-refund' buttons. REGRESSION: legacy data-testid='order-refund-btn-*' (⊗ Refund) and data-testid='order-refire-btn-*' (✉ Refire) still render alongside the new controls. Seed cs_test_agent1/2 deleted, mountain-range-silhouette in_stock reset to 4 at teardown.
action_items: No defects. The known refund-SUCCESS path against real Stripe/PayPal was not exercised per main-agent guidance (shared code with no_refund + pre-existing refund helpers).
Cloudflare 1010 blocks urllib on this preview host — admin JWT minting from CI-style callers must use `requests` (or a real browser UA). Not an app defect, but worth documenting in the ops runbook.
critical_code_review_comments: order_cancellation.py _lock_cancellation (L86-94): elegant atomic idempotency via find_one_and_update with $nin ACTIVE_STATUSES — no race window, no double-refund possible. Solid pattern.

order_cancellation.py _execute refund-failure branch (L221-240): correctly writes refund_failed to DB, pushes timeline event, fires admin alert, then raises 409 (not 502) so Cloudflare doesn't swallow the JSON body. Comment inline explains the choice — nice touch.

order_cancellation.py admin_reopen (L350-377): rolls back inventory when it was restored (decrementing both variant.$.in_stock and the top-level in_stock). This is critical to avoid double-adds when the same order is cancelled → reopened → cancelled again — good.

order_cancellation.py _restore_inventory (L97-114): correctly guards with tracks_inventory != False (default true) and handles variant_id. Restoration is idempotent-per-cancel because the lock prevents re-entry.

cancellation-stats (L380-417): the buyer_requested/mutual initiator remapping via reason_group is a nice UX detail — makes it clear who's driving cancellations even when the maker fires the endpoint on behalf of the buyer.

Minor: _send_emails swallows all exceptions (L263-264) — this is correct (emails must not block the state transition), but the WARNING log line is the only signal. Consider a metric/alert if email failures cross a threshold.

PaidOrdersList.jsx renders `⊗ Refund` and `⊘ No-refund` side by side on open orders — visually both destructive. Consider distinct colors (Refund=red, No-refund=amber/warning) so operators don't mis-click. Not blocking, but worth an accessibility pass.

CancelOrderModal.jsx: two-step nudge (contact-buyer-btn → cancel-continue) is a great friction gate. Note-to-buyer and internal-note are properly separated (maker sees note_to_buyer only). Looks clean.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 3 review-request UI bullets verified — maker actions/modal/timeline, admin stats/badges/no-refund/edit/reopen, regression)

Pre-existing cs_test_cxl1 (open/reopened) and cs_test_cxl2 (canceled_no_refund, reason 'buyer-requested', note 'Chargeback CB-9931') left in place per main-agent note — used as the cancelled-state UI fixture.

rca of the issue: N/A — no defects found. Every review-request bullet passed on first execution. The atomic $nin ACTIVE_STATUSES lock + timeline-append pattern makes the whole workflow robust against duplicate cancellations, and the refund-failure branch correctly separates the failure state (order stays open, admin alert fires) from the success state (order marked canceled, buyer + maker + admin emails).
